Stochastic Block Models for Multiplex networks: application

War and Alliance case study

team großBM

2026-11-06

Source: vignettes/Multiplex_allianceNwar_case_study.qmd

1. Preliminaries

This vignette illustrates the use of the estimateMultiplexSBM function and the methods accompanying the R6 class MultiplexSBM_fit on the war data set. The models are described in the vignette Stochastic Block Models for Multiplex networks: principle.

The packages required for the analysis are sbm plus some others for data manipulation and representation:

library(sbm)
library(igraph)
library(aricode)
library(knitr)
library(patchwork) # to put figures side by side

To display the composition of the clusters, we use the following function, which gives a table with the names of the nodes of each cluster in a column:

clusterComposition <- function(memberships, nodeNames) {
  clusters <- split(nodeNames, factor(memberships, levels = 1:max(memberships)))
  maxSize  <- max(lengths(clusters))
  tab <- sapply(clusters, function(x) c(x, rep("", maxSize - length(x))))
  colnames(tab) <- paste("Cluster", seq_along(clusters))
  as.data.frame(tab)
}

2. Data set

2.1 Description of the data

The war data set comes in the sbm package:

data("war")

This data set contains a list of two networks (belligerent and alliance) where the nodes are countries; an edge in the network belligerent means that the two countries have been at war at least once between years 1816 to 2007; an edge in network alliance means that the two countries have had a formal alliance between years 1816 and 2012. The network belligerent has less nodes since countries which have not been at war at all are not considered.

These two networks were extracted from https://correlatesofwar.org/ (see Sarkees and Wayman (2010) for war data, and Gibler (2008) for formal alliance). Version 4.0 was used for war data and version 4.1 for formal alliance.

2.2 Data manipulation

Since they don’t have the same size, we choose to only consider nodes (countries) which were at war with at least one other country. This corresponds to the first 83 nodes in the Alliance network.

A <- as_adjacency_matrix(war$alliance, sparse = FALSE)
A <- A[1:83, 1:83]
B <- as_adjacency_matrix(war$belligerent, sparse = FALSE)

We can start with a plot of this multiplex network:

netA <- defineSBM(A, model = "bernoulli", dimLabels = "country")
netB <- defineSBM(B, model = "bernoulli", dimLabels = "country")
listNet <- list(Alliance = netA, Belligerence = netB)
plotMyMultiplexMatrix(listNet)

3. Multiplex SBM with independent layers

We run the estimation of this multiplex model. By setting dependent = FALSE, we declare that we consider the two layers to be independent conditionally on the latent block variables.

The multiplex SBM with independent layers

Denoting Y1Y^1 the alliance network and Y2Y^2 the war network, the n=83n = 83 countries are divided into QQ blocks with proportions π\pi and, for ℓ=1,2\ell = 1, 2, Yijℓ∣Zi=q,Zj=r∼indℬern(αqrℓ). Y^\ell_{ij} \mid Z_i = q, Z_j = r \sim_{ind} \mathcal{B}ern(\alpha^\ell_{qr}).

MultiplexFitIndep <- estimateMultiplexSBM(listNet, dependent = FALSE,
    estimOptions = list(verbosity = 0))

We can retrieve the clustering:

clust_country_indep <- MultiplexFitIndep$memberships[[1]]
kable(clusterComposition(clust_country_indep, rownames(A)),
      caption = "Country clusters (independent layers)")

And we can plot the reorganized adjacency matrices, or the graphon, i.e. the estimated connectivities α̂qrℓ\widehat{\alpha}^\ell_{qr} alone: each block is represented by an interval whose length is its estimated proportion π̂q\widehat{\pi}_q, and the rectangle q×rq \times r of the layer ℓ\ell is colored according to α̂qrℓ\widehat{\alpha}^\ell_{qr}, the two layers sharing the same color scale. The graphon is close to the plot of the expectations (type = "expected"), which colors each pair of countries (i,j)(i,j) with ∑q,rτ̂iqτ̂jrα̂qrℓ\sum_{q,r} \widehat{\tau}_{iq}\widehat{\tau}_{jr}\widehat{\alpha}^\ell_{qr}, τ̂iq\widehat{\tau}_{iq} being the estimated probability that country ii belongs to block qq: the two plots coincide when the clustering is clear-cut, but the graphon only depends on the parameters, not on the nodes.

plot(MultiplexFitIndep)
plot(MultiplexFitIndep, type = "graphon")

4. Multiplex SBM with dependent layers

Now we assume that the two layers are dependent conditionally to the latent block variables. We then set dependent = TRUE.

The multiplex SBM with dependent layers

Conditionally to the blocks, the pair (Yij1,Yij2)(Y^1_{ij}, Y^2_{ij}) follows a bivariate Bernoulli distribution: for any ω=(ω1,ω2)∈{0,1}2\omega = (\omega_1, \omega_2) \in \{0,1\}^2, ℙ((Yij1,Yij2)=ω∣Zi=q,Zj=r)=αqrω, \mathbb{P}\left((Y^1_{ij}, Y^2_{ij}) = \omega \mid Z_i = q, Z_j = r\right) = \alpha^{\omega}_{qr}, with αqr00+αqr01+αqr10+αqr11=1\alpha^{00}_{qr} + \alpha^{01}_{qr} + \alpha^{10}_{qr} + \alpha^{11}_{qr} = 1. These probabilities are stored in connectParam$prob00, connectParam$prob01, connectParam$prob10 and connectParam$prob11.

MultiplexFitdep <- estimateMultiplexSBM(listNet, dependent = TRUE,
    estimOptions = list(verbosity = 0))

We can retrieve the clustering and compare it to the one obtained in the independent case.

clust_country_dep <- MultiplexFitdep$memberships[[1]]
kable(clusterComposition(clust_country_dep, rownames(A)),
      caption = "Country clusters (dependent layers)")

plotAlluvial(list(independent = clust_country_indep, dependent = clust_country_dep))

From independent to dependent, the model gathers blocks 3 and 2, i.e put together all the countries of Latino and south America.

On top of the clustering comparison, we can compare the ICL criterion to see which of the dependent or independent models is a best fit:

MultiplexFitdep$ICL
#> [1] -1470.276
MultiplexFitIndep$ICL
#> [1] -1434.602

We can do the same plots for the reorganized matrices and the graphon. Note that the graphon represents the marginal connectivity of each layer, α̂qr10+α̂qr11\widehat{\alpha}^{10}_{qr} + \widehat{\alpha}^{11}_{qr} for the alliances and α̂qr01+α̂qr11\widehat{\alpha}^{01}_{qr} + \widehat{\alpha}^{11}_{qr} for the wars, and it may be relevant to have a look at the conditional probabilities.

plot(MultiplexFitdep)
plot(MultiplexFitdep, type = "graphon")

For instance, we may want to compare, for two countries in given blocks, the probability of having been at war while being allied at some point (before or after), αqr11/(αqr11+αqr10)\alpha^{11}_{qr} / (\alpha^{11}_{qr} + \alpha^{10}_{qr}), to the marginal probability of having been at war, αqr11+αqr01\alpha^{11}_{qr} + \alpha^{01}_{qr}:

p11 <- MultiplexFitdep$connectParam$prob11
p01 <- MultiplexFitdep$connectParam$prob01
p10 <- MultiplexFitdep$connectParam$prob10
round(p11/(p11 + p10), 2)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,] 0.01 0.14 0.03 0.43
#> [2,] 0.14 0.11 0.09 0.10
#> [3,] 0.03 0.09 0.05 0.03
#> [4,] 0.43 0.10 0.03 0.09

These two matrices can be represented as graphons, side by side with patchwork, on the same color scale:

pCond <- p11/(p11 + p10) # conditional probabilities of being at war while having been or will
# be allied
pMarg <- p11 + p01 # marginal probabilities of being at war
limits <- c(0, max(pCond, pMarg))
optGraphon <- list(limits = limits, legend = TRUE, legend.title = TRUE)
gCond <- plotMyGraphon(pCond, MultiplexFitdep$blockProp, nbNodes = 83, dimLabels = "country",
  plotOptions = c(optGraphon, title = "P(war | alliance)"))
gMarg <- plotMyGraphon(pMarg, MultiplexFitdep$blockProp, nbNodes = 83, dimLabels = "country",
  plotOptions = c(optGraphon, title = "P(war)"))
(gCond | gMarg) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
  ggplot2::labs(fill = "Probability") & ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

References

Gibler, Douglas M. 2008. International Military Alliances, 1648-2008. CQ Press.
Sarkees, Meredith Reid, and Frank Whelon Wayman. 2010. Resort to War: A Data Guide to Inter-State, Extra-State, Intra-State, and Non-State Wars, 1816-2007. Cq Pr.
